## Reconstruction complete

**Implemented in `solution.py`** (single executable script, no external deps beyond numpy; reproducible from a clean state in ~1.5 s on CPU).

### Approach taken

Three general-purpose regularisation methods, all expressed as minimisation/iteration in the original `x` space (no pre-chosen basis, no Fourier/polynomial/wavelet/dictionary representation):

| folder alias A | folder alias B | method | reg-param chosen by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method_a` | `tikhonov` | Tikhonov L2 | Hansen-style discrete L-curve corner (max |κ| on the (log‖x‖, log‖r‖) curve, 200-pt log-spaced α grid), with Morozov-discrepancy α reported as a sanity check |
| `method_b` | `tsvd` | Truncated SVD | Smallest k with ‖r_k‖ ≤ τ·‖noise‖, τ = 1 (Morozov); prefer smaller k on ties |
| `method_c` | `cgls` | CGLS (iterative Krylov) | Smallest iter with ‖r_k‖ ≤ τ·‖noise‖, τ = 1 (Morozov) |

All three share one SVD, one noise estimate, and one comparison module — single source of truth, written to both naming conventions so the two folder hierarchies never drift.

### Diagnostic numbers

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---:|
| σ_noise per orthonormal component | **0.026844** |
| ‖noise‖ (Parseval, √m·σ_n) | **0.399965** |
| effective rank from Picard transition | **32** |
| dpc_judgment | **does_not_hold** |
| log₁₀(σ_min/σ_max) | −14.76 (cond(K) ≈ 5.7 × 10¹⁴) |
| geometric ratio of K singular spectrum | **σ_k = 0.8574620978ᵏ** (exact) |

### Method results

| Method | reg-param | ‖Kx − y‖ | ‖x‖ | ‖∇x‖₂ | ‖∇x‖∞ | sens (−) | sens (+) | norm-sum |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A — Tikhonov (L-curve) | α = 1.804186e−02 | 0.4757 | 2.6939 | 1.93 | 0.467 | 0.057 | 0.044 | 157.93 |
| B — TSVD (Morozov)    | k = 33              | 0.3984 | 10.041 | 6.40 | 1.370 | 0.620 | 0.541 | 17.73 |
| C — CGLS (Morozov)    | iter = 26           | 0.3995 | 8.027  | 4.94 | 0.880 | 0.059 | 0.010 | **5.011** |

Pareto check shows **B is dominated by C** (C better on all three criteria); **A and C are both Pareto-optimal**. The normalised-sum rule (smaller is better) selects **Method C (CGLS, Morozov)** as the recommended solution.

### Justification
- C achieves ‖r‖ ≈ ‖noise‖ exactly (|Δr| = 5 × 10⁻⁴) — residual is essentially pure noise, the data-driven Morozov priori is fully respected.
- The high-i β tail (e.g. i = 200, ratio ≈ 4.7 × 10¹⁰) shows DPC does not hold globally, but the Morozov prior on noise projection (≈ 0.027 per orthonormal component) matches the high-i β tail beautifully.
- C also has Tikhonov-comparable perturbation sensitivity (~6 %) while delivering far better fit. The L-curve α (Method A) corresponds to an over-regularised solution (‖r‖ ≈ 0.48 vs ‖noise‖ ≈ 0.40), because the geometric SVD makes the L-curve very flat near the elbow and forces a more conservative choice — a known L-curve pathology for severely ill-posed operators, reported transparently rather than forced into agreement.
- C and A both store x as a single 222-vector written to two paths. Recommended solution is byte-identical to method_c/cgls/x_reg.csv.

### Files written (all 19 verified present)

```
solution.py
results/diagnosis/picard_data.csv                        222 data rows + header, 3 cols
results/diagnosis/diagnosis_report.md                    noise/eff_rank/dpc structured
results/solution/method_a/x_reg.csv, reg_param.txt, lcurve_data.csv   ← mirrored to
results/solution/tikhonov/x_reg.csv, reg_param.txt, lcurve_data.csv   ← tikhonov
results/solution/method_b/x_reg.csv, reg_param.txt        ← mirrored to
results/solution/tsvd/x_reg.csv, reg_param.txt           ← tsvd
results/solution/method_c/x_reg.csv, reg_param.txt       ← mirrored to
results/solution/cgls/x_reg.csv, reg_param.txt           ← cgls
results/comparison/comparison_report.md                  full analysis + Pareto + norm-sum
results/comparison/recommended_solution.csv              == method_c/cgls (CGLS winner)
```

Mirror integrity confirmed by SHA-256: `method_a` ↔ `tikhonov` share hash prefix `876476520b`; `method_b` ↔ `tsvd` share `f5ebdcc4c2`; `method_c` ↔ `cgls` share `957f25b1f7`. `recommended_solution.csv` also hash `957f25b1f7` (CGLS winner).

### Reproducibility
`rm -rf results && python3 solution.py` produces all 19 files in ~1.5 s with byte-identical solutions each run.

### Known limitations
- The L-curve criterion, applied to this geometric SVD, lands ~2 decades above the Morozov α — a documented pathology of L-curve for very smooth, severely ill-posed operators. Reflected honestly in the report rather than forced into agreement.
- Morozov τ = 1.0 uses the i.i.d. white-noise assumption to set ‖noise‖ = √m·σ_n. The high-i |β_i|² tail is very flat (no trend), supporting this assumption.
- Effective rank = 32 is defined by the rule "first i such that |β_i|/σ_i > 10·geometric_mean(|β_j|/σ_j, j<10)" — adapted from low-mode Picard diagnostics.
- The mirror writes assume `_write_mirrored_data` receives a single in-memory dict; any future change to one method propagates automatically to both folder aliases.
